plan: Given my value of $13, I need to consider a bidding strategy that maximizes profit. Since this is the first and only round, I don't have historical data to learn from other bidders' tendencies. The optimal strategy in a first-price sealed-bid auction with N bidders and values drawn uniformly from [0, V] is to bid (N-1)/N * V_i. In this case, N=3, and the maximum value is $49. So, my optimal bid would be (3-1)/3 * 13 = 2/3 * 13 = 8.66. I will round this to the nearest 0.1 increment.

This is the first round, so there's no history to learn from. My value is $15. To maximize profit, I want to win the item for a price just above the second-highest bid. Since I don't know the other players' values or bidding strategies, a common initial strategy is to bid a fraction of my value or slightly below my value. Given the value range of $0-$49, and my value being $15, I will bid slightly below my value to ensure a positive profit if I win, while still having a reasonable chance of winning. I'll bid $14.90.

I have a high private value of $47. Since this is the first and only round, I need to maximize my profit in this single instance. Given the payment rule (pay highest competing bid), I want to bid just above what I anticipate others might bid, but not so high that I significantly reduce my profit if I win.
